MSc Mathematics is a 2-year postgraduate course in Mathematics dealing with providing in-depth knowledge of advanced and applied mathematics like geometry, algebra, calculus, number theory, dynamical systems, and differential equations and preparing them for various research activities. To be eligible for the course, the student must complete his/her graduation from a recognized university with a minimum of 50% score. However, students having a B.Sc./B.Tech./B.E. degrees are preferred. However, some colleges organize their admission tests which the students have to clear if they wish to become a part of that particular college. Some of the subjects that come under the MSc in Mathematics Syllabus are Real Analysis, Algebra, Number Theory, Probability Theory, etc. The course also includes general subjects like Physics and Chemistry. MSc deals with the advanced concepts of Mathematics. It incorporates mathematical thinking in the minds of the students. There are plenty of colleges and universities offering this course like St. Xavier’s College, Alagappa University, St. Stephens College, and many more. You can also pursue this course from distance learning colleges like IGNOU, Periyar University, and others. The application forms are released in both online and offline mode and the students will be notified about it from the official website of the University. For most colleges, the admission process is direct and the students are admitted based on the marks acquired by them on graduation. However, in some colleges, the students will have to appear for an additional entrance test. Here we have mentioned the various steps of admission. Direct Admission Aspirants will fill the application form, from where they will have to give their necessary details category proof, qualification details, and many other things, and then they have to submit the form. Then shortlisting of candidates will be done on the basis of the cutoff list released by the colleges. Those students who will clear the cutoff will be called for further admission process. Entrance Examination Colleges offering admissions on the basis of entrance exam scores have a different process. Firstly, they have to fill-up the form to register for the exams available on the official website of the university. Then they have to appear for the entrance test. The details and mode of the entrance test may vary from university to university. The students may be called for an additional round of personal interviews prior to their admission to the institute. Then on the basis of the final score of entrance exam and PI, admissions will be offered to the student. Lateral Entry A few of the colleges admit students through lateral entry. Through lateral entry, admissions will be directly given to the second year of the course. Two such colleges are IIT Delhi and IIT Kanpur. The Eligibility criterion for admission through lateral entry is the same including graduation degree with mathematics as a mandatory subject. MSc Maths First Semester Subjects Algebra: Algebra deals with symbols and the rules for manipulating those symbols, which represent quantities without fixed values, called variables Topology: The arrangement of nodes and connections within a network is called topology. It explains how a network is connected, and how the information in the network flows. Real Analysis: Real Analysis formalizes the study of numbers and functions and investigates important concepts such as limits and continuity. See Also: Maths Courses MSc Maths Second Semester Subjects Complex Analysis: Complex analysis is the study of complex numbers together with their derivatives, manipulation, and other properties. Complex analysis is an extremely powerful tool with an unexpectedly large number of practical applications to the solution of physical problems. Functional Analysis: Functional analysis is a model of a psychological formulation designed to understand the functions of human behavior. It has its origins in behavioral psychology. At its core, the functional analysis assumes that all behavior is learned and that all behaviors serve some purpose. Partial Differential Equations: A partial differential equation is one of the types of differential equations, it contains unknown multi-variables with their partial derivatives. See Also: Quantitative Modelling Courses MSc Maths Third Semester Subjects Differential Geometry: Differential geometry studies the geometry of smooth shapes and smooth spaces or smooth manifolds. Mathematical Methods: Mathematical methods include the Finite Difference Method, Numerical Model, Electromagnetism, Boundary Condition, Continuum, Hydrodynamics, Water Distribution System and Genetic Algorithm. Numerical Analysis: Numerical analysis solves continuous problems using numeric approximation. It involves designing methods, useful in cases where the exact solution is impossible to calculate. See Also: Numerology Courses MSc Maths Fourth Semester Subjects Measure And Integration: Measure and Integration studies that smaller functions have smaller integrals, and that two integrable functions having the same integral over every set are almost equal. What are the questions asked in an interview for an integrated PhD (maths) at IISc Bangalore? ● Top Answer By Monika Saha on 18 Jul 23 Ans. One of my friends appeared for the integrated Ph.D. Math at IISc Bangalore and shared her experience of the same. A total of 72 students had been shortlisted for the interview and her interview took place on the last day. As she entered the room, they asked for her introduction and her interest to which she told them it was analysis. She was asked the following questions Construct a differential function satisfying the following conditions, f(1)=f(-1)=o; f(0)=1, and f(x) is zero everywhere except (-1, 1) Group theory question wherein they gave her an order of the group and asked to check the elements of some order The entire interview was based on the above questions which my friend was not able to answer most of the time and thus did not get selected. However, she learned a lot from that interview and summed the entire experience in these points She learned a new problem-solving approach that requires breaking the problem into small cases. The panelists here are very friendly and you can even postpone your interview till the last day if you are not comfortable. The questions asked to a candidate are never repeated for other candidates. So, overall the experience was very knowledgeable and I hope it's so for you too. Read more 0 0 Share Facebook Twitter Copy Link 1 Answer ●●● Upvote Downvote Report Ques. MSc Physics is a two-year-long postgraduate-level course in India. MSc Physics eligibility requires candidates to have a minimum of 50% marks in their bachelor's degree (preferably BSc Physics Hons.) from a recognized university. Admission to most of the top MSc Physics colleges in India like Hindu College, Hansraj College, Fergusson College, Ramjas College, etc is taken through entrance exams. Some of the popular entrances for MSc Physics admission are CUET, IPU CET, OUCET, BITSAT, BHU PET, etc The MSc Physics Syllabus covers 10 different domains of Physics, including quantum mechanics, astrophysics, optics, and nuclear physics, among others. One can pursue an MSc Physics distance education from colleges like Annamalai University, Alagappa University, Madurai Kamaraj University, etc within the maximum duration of 5 years. The eligibility criteria for the course to be studied from a distance are the same as the criteria required for a regular course. However, admission is offered based on merit. Admission Criteria Merit and Entrance Exams MSc Mathematics Entrance Exams IIT JAM, CUET, NEST, CUCET, etc. Tuition Fee INR 5,000 - INR 20,000 (Government Colleges) Starting Salary INR 2 - 5 Lakhs per annum MSc Mathematics Jobs Research scientists, Teachers, Data analysts, and others Top Recruiting Companies Wipro, IBM India, HCL Technologies, Larsen & Toubro (L&T), Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), etc. MSc Physics Eligibility MSc physics eligibility criteria for admission are discussed below: A candidate should come to the course after a minimum of 10+2+3 years of continuous study. To be eligible for most universities, a candidate must have a BSc physics Honours degree with a minimum of 50% marks in graduation, but some very good universities also demand 55% marks. However, some universities like Delhi University also grant admission to candidates with BSc in electronics, mathematics, and engineering graduates. The minimum mark criteria for these candidates seeking admission to Delhi University is 60%. MSc Physics Admission Process in India Admission to this course in most of the top MSc physics colleges like IIT Kharagpur, Miranda House, IIT Bombay, NIT Nagaland, and more is done based on marks obtained in the entrance test. Following are the basic steps any candidates need to take for MSc physics admission 2024: Application for the course: The first step for admission to MSc physics courses is applying for the course through the application portal of the university. Most universities provide a joint application form for both the entrance exam and the course application. However, for universities like JNU, entrance exams are conducted by NTA, and the candidates will have to apply through the NTA website also. Entrance Exam: Entrance exams are compulsory for most of the top universities. A candidate willing to be admitted for the MSc physics course must qualify for the entrance examination. Many universities like NIT Nagaland, JNU, and BHU, have their entrance examination, while some colleges like Fergusson College, Ramjas College, etc take admission through common entrance exams. Merit list and Counseling: After the results of entrance examinations are published, the universities release a list of successful candidates who are called for document verification. A candidate must regularly check the university website for updates on this issue. Interview and Enrollment: This is the final step in the admission process in which a candidate needs to appear for an interview. The interviewer may or may not ask subject-based questions to the candidates, depending on the policies of the institution. At this step, the candidate must also present all the original transcripts and other essential documents required to establish his eligibility. After his eligibility is proven, he is granted admission to the course. A part of the MSc Physics Syllabus includes seminars, lectures, workshops, and practical lab work. Also, students will be required to complete a research project towards the last two semesters and this forms an integral part of the MSc Physics syllabus. In the final examination, class assignments, end-semester exams, internships, and project reports are also considered. There might be variations in the MSc Physics subjects from college to college. MSc Computer Science is a two-year post-graduation program to develop advanced programming skills and strategies to solve various logical challenges using different programming languages. MSc Computer Science or MSc CS focuses more on developing software and networking-based skills. There are a lot of career opportunities after completing an M.Sc in Computer Science such as working as a Networking Master, Software Developer, Tester, Web Developer, Cryptography, etc. MSc in Computer Science is one of the most pursued computer courses to get good jobs in India. The MSc Computer Science syllabus is divided into two years and each year of study comprises two semesters. Some of the major MSc Computer Science subjects are Advanced Programming Language, Operating Systems, Data Structures using C, Artificial Intelligence, Microprocessors and Applications, Advanced Computer Networks, System Software, and Data Networking. One can also opt for MSc Computer Science distance education. IGNOU, Alagappa University, etc, are some of the top universities offering MSc Computer Science through distance. M.Sc in computer science is a career-making course for computer enthusiasts. Aspirants with bachelor's degrees in computer science, computer applications, and others are drawn and attracted to this course. The continuous & remarkable growth in the digital front has resulted in the growing popularity of various courses in the field of technology. Computer Science is one such area in which the education sector takes great interest. See Also: MSc Computer Science and Technology M.Sc. Computer Science or Master of Science in Computing may be a two-year post-graduate program. The M.Sc. in computing course is meant to equip you with the knowledge and skills to develop innovative solutions that the fashionable computing industry requires. See Also: Computer Science Courses Computer Science is one of the foremost popular specializations of the Master of Science degree and therefore the course of M.Sc computing is obtainable in several institutes in both regular as well as distance mode. Why Study MSc Computer Science? The range of computing applications and their importance to our way of life has expanded rapidly and gained more importance in recent years. There are many developments in artificial life in various fields like computer vision, robotics, mobile devices, and game applications that have all become a normal part of our interactions with computing devices. Who Should Study MSc Computer Science? One must have the ability to create and invent things, good knowledge of technology, and an interest in mathematics and science. One should be familiar with programming and computer hardware/software. One should have good analytical skills, an eye for details sustained attention, and the ability to solve problems. One should possess good communication skills, be proficient in analyzing and evaluating data, and have the skill to make decisions, work in teams, and express their ideas both orally and in writing. MSc Zoology is a 2-year postgraduate study dedicated to the study of animals. The program dives deep into the biology, behavior, and structure of animals. Any candidate who wishes to pursue a Master of Science in Zoology should have a bachelor's degree in Medical Sciences, Allied Sciences, Biosciences, or any Life Sciences specialization. They should have scored at least 50% marks at the undergraduate level from a recognized university. It is a two-year postgraduate zoology program, consisting of 4 semesters. Admissions are either based on merit or through entrance exams conducted at the university level. Some of the institutes also hold a personal interview round as part of the admission process. The average tuition fee of the MSc in Zoology program is around INR 21,000 to INR 1.5 lacs annually. MSc Zoology Syllabus focuses on an in-depth study of animal tissues, structures, etc. After completing the MSc Zoology course, candidates can pursue a career as a zoologist and earn an average salary of 3 – 4 LPA. Top Recruiting Companies College/Universities, Zoo and National Park, Agricultural Sector, Food Park, Plant Research Centre, etc Job Positions Zookeeper, Wildlife Rehabilitator, Zoology Teacher, Wildlife Educator, Research Associate, etc MSc Zoology Admission Process The top institutes in the country that offer MSc Zoology admit students either on the basis of an entrance examination or on the basis of previous academic records. The dates for the entrance exams are announced quite earlier. To secure admission into MSc Zoology, the following steps can be referred to. Step 1: Look out for the entrance examination notice of the institute you choose to apply to. Dates for registration will be announced in advance by the institutes. Step 2: Register for the examination and appear for it. Look for the syllabus and the past papers, if available. Practicing in a timely manner will be useful for the final examination. Step 3: If the candidate qualifies the examination and scores above the minimum cut-off, then they will be invited for an interview round. Step 4: Appear for the personal interview. Interviews are usually conducted with the department heads of the institute or college. Step 5: Candidates who have passed the personal interview round, will be given an offer letter for admission. They will have to pay the admission fee within the provided time, to book their seat in the program. MSc Zoology Eligibility Criteria The candidates are required to meet the eligibility criteria set by the institutes to apply for admission. The general criteria followed by most institutes are mentioned below: The candidate should have a B.Sc. degree in Zoology or other Allied Medical Sciences, with at least 50% aggregate marks from a recognized institute. The candidate should have completed their 10+2 examinations from a state-recognized board. MSc Zoology Entrance Exams Institutes usually conduct their own entrance examination for this program. Some of the popular examinations at the top institutes are as follows: PUET: Pune University conducts an entrance exam for admission into its M.Sc. Zoology program. The examination is usually conducted in the month of June. Applications for the same are accepted from April and May. Christ University Assessment Test: Christ University conducts a skills assessment test to admit students in the M.Sc. Zoology program. The examination tests candidates in written skills, communication skills, and logical reasoning. Upon passing the entrance examination, candidates will be invited for a personal interview round. Most of the institutes do not have a prover syllabus set for its entrance examinations. Some of the expected topics are mentioned below: Biomolecules: structure, organization, and role Cell Structure and function Cell Signalling Immunology Genetics Animal and Plant Physiology Ecology It is not very tough to solve MSc Zoology exams. The entrance examinations cover the material taught in the graduation level of B.Sc. Zoology program. So, candidates holding bachelors in zoology can clear it only by studying their course topics. It would be beneficial to look at the previous question papers, to get an idea of the exam you are applying. Solving model test papers can help to practice and check the amount of preparation done. How to get admission in a good MSc Zoology college? If admission is merit-based, a high score at the undergraduate level is required. The candidate should meet the minimum cut-off prescribed by the college. Colleges advertise when seats are available and when admission season opens up. All the latest admission advertisements must be viewed regularly. For admission through entrance examinations, going through the undergraduate course material in zoology as well as general knowledge, latest news, and basic mathematics is recommended. Most colleges hold a personal interview round where students who have cleared the entrance examinations are invited. Candidates must prepare diligently for this round. Preparations must be started at least 6 months prior to the examination date to make time to cover all material. MSc Zoology: What is it about? Candidates with a B.Sc. degree in Zoology or other Allied Medical Sciences often opt for M.Sc. Zoology. It is the best program for the one who wishes to pursue a career related to animals. M.Sc. in Zoology covers a wide range of subjects that deals with the study of the animal kingdom including their biology, genetics, classification, evolution, and many more. Graduates from this program find employment as researchers, teachers, professors, zoologists, zoo animal welfare, etc. Candidates in this program get to learn about the basics of zoology like biochemistry and genetics. During the later semesters, one can choose specializations to study with their course load. The program helps students work in animal biodiversity, bioinformatics, ecosystem monitoring, wildlife conservation, etc. Why study MSc Zoology? Students who choose to do masters in zoology may see that there are many benefits of studying this program. Some of the benefits are: Diverse career options: An M.Sc. Zoology graduates can find jobs in numerous sectors after graduation. They can work as professors of zoology, work as researchers, animal trainers, wildlife experts, etc. Jobs are available in both the private and public sectors. High salary: Due to the high number of job options available, the salary offered to candidates is also high. For fresh graduates, the salary ranges up to INR 2 lacs p.a. syllabus.text: MSc Zoology Syllabus Semester I Semster II Structure and Functions of Non-chordates Structure and Functions of Chordates Ecological theories and applications Comparative Animal Physiology Genetics and Genetic Engineering Endocrinology and Neuroscience Tissue structure Function and Chemistry Cell and Receptor Biology Parasites and Immunity Biochemistry and Molecular biology Laboratory course Laboratory course Semester III Semster IV Development and Differentiation Conservation Biology and Wildlife Taxonomy and Biodiversity Laboratory course Elective I Theory Biotechnology and Applications Elective I Practical Elective II Theory Evolution and Animal Behaviour Biostatistics, Bioinformatics, and Instrumentation Laboratory course Elective II Practical MSc Zoology Semester Wise Syllabus MSc Zoology has 2 semesters each year for 2 years. The subjects are explained below: MSc Zoology First Semester Subjects Ecological theories and applications: The theory of ecology includes the heterogeneous distribution of organisms, interactions of organisms, the mortality of organisms, contingency, environmental heterogeneity finite and heterogeneous resources and evolutionary cause of ecological properties. Genetics and Genetic Engineering: Genetic engineering is called as a process, where laboratory-based technologies are used to alter the DNA makeup of an organism. Tissue structure Function and Chemistry: A group of cells that have a similar structures and that function together as a unit is known as tissue. See Also Ecology Courses Genetics Courses MSc Zoology Second Semester Subjects Comparative Animal Physiology: It involves physiology where processes of vertebrates and invertebrates are studied at the cellular, organ and whole animal levels of the organization. Endocrinology and Neuroscience: Neuroscience is the study of the brain and nervous system. While Endocrinology is the study of hormones. Here, the study of interactions between hormones and the brain, primarily how hormones affect behavior are studied. Cell and Receptor Biology: This subject is about cellular receptors. They are proteins either inside a cell or on its surface, which receive a signal. See Also: Neurology Courses Neuroscience Courses MSc Zoology Third Semester Subjects Development and Differentiation: Differentiation refers to the normal process by which a less specialized cell undergoes maturation to become more distinct in form and Developmental biology means a process by which animals and plants grow and develop. Taxonomy and Biodiversity: Taxonomy defines the places to which they belong. It provides an easy to identify the categories of the species and to plan necessary measures for biodiversity conservation. Evolution and Animal Behaviour: It is the study of the behaviors controlled by genes, they may evolve through natural selection. MSc Zoology Fourth Semester Conservation Biology and Wildlife: A practice of protecting plant and animal species and their habitats. Wildlife provides nature processes balance and stability. MSc Biotechnology is a 2-year postgraduate degree program that focuses on the application of biological processes to develop new products and technologies in various fields like healthcare, agriculture, food, energy, and environment. Biotechnology involves using living organisms or their products to improve and develop processes, products, and technologies. MSc Biotechnology subjects include Biological Chemistry, Genetic Engineering, Environmental Biotechnology, Bacteriology and Virology, Plant Biotechnology, Molecular Biology, Immunology, Cell Biology etc. Also, MSc Biotechnology Colleges include JNU, BHU, University of Calcutta, etc. The average fees in Top MSc Biotechnology Colleges are INR 2,000 to INR 60,000. MSc Biotechnology eligibility is to have a bachelor's degree in science with a specialization in any biological sciences. Graduates from BAMS, BHMS, BPT, and BPharm. are also eligible for admission. At least 50% must have been scored in aggregate at the undergraduate level. MSc Biotechnology jobs include roles like Research Biochemist, Biotechnology Researcher, Associate Engineer, Quality Controller etc. MSc in Biotechnology salary for freshers ranges between INR 3,50,000 to INR 5,40,000. Environmental Biotechnology: Environmental Biotechnology addresses environmental problems, such as the genetic rescue of a species, the removal of pollution, renewable energy generation or biomass production. Molecular Biology: Molecular biology studies the molecular basis of biological activity. Molecular biologist studies how molecules interact with one another in living organisms to perform the functions of life. Genetic Engineering: Genetic engineering is a process that uses laboratory-based technologies to alter the DNA of an organism. Plant Biotechnology: Plant biotechnology is used to adapt plants for specific opportunities. Situations that combine multiple needs and opportunities are common. See Also: Biotechnology Certificate Courses Medical Biotechnology Courses Biotechnology Courses After 12th MSc Biotechnology Syllabus: Second Year Subjects Animal Biotechnology: Animal biotechnology is used to genetically engineer animals in order to improve their suitability for agriculture, industrial, or pharmaceutical applications. Bioprocess engineering & Fermentation Technology: Bioprocess or fermentation technology involves complete living cells, organelles or enzymes as the biocatalyst, and aim to bring specific chemical and/or physical changes in biochemical. Bioinformatics: Bioinformatics is the application of tools of computation and analysis to the capture and interpretation of biological data. Genomics and Proteomics: Genomics is the study of the entire set of genes in the genome of a cell, and proteomics studies the entire set of proteins produced by the cell. Nanobiotechnology: Nanobiotechnology is a multi-strategic technique that combines nanotechnology and biotechnology to engineer the properties of therapeutic agents. MSc Microbiology is a 2 year advanced postgraduate course that combines the disciplines of chemistry and biology. MSc Microbiology can be studied after completing graduation in the fields of Botany, Zoology, Chemistry, Physiology and Microbiology. MSc Microbiology studies the relationship of biology and chemistry with the environment and it’s ecosystem. A minimum MSc Microbiology eligibility is to have a BSc degree with a minimum of 50% or more from a recognized university to apply for the MSc Microbiology course. Admission to MSc Microbiology colleges Delhi University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, etc are offered generally on the basis of marks obtained in the entrances. Some of the popular entrances are IPU CET, CUET, etc. The course is divided into 4 semesters which cover different aspects of the programs including biostatistics, immunology, virology etc. Every student getting enrolled for the programme needs to go through several research works and laboratory sessions as well. Admission to MSc Microbiology in India is offered on the basis of the Common Entrance Test (CET) mechanism like IPU CET, OUCET, BITSAT, etc. These tests measure the aptitude of students for MSc Microbiology. Delhi University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, Banaras Hindu University, etc are some of the popular universities conducting their own entrance for MSc Microbiology admission. The admission process is further followed by a round of counseling and personal interview. Given below are the steps for MSc Microbiology admission 2024: Step 1: Check the eligibility for the respective entrances and apply for the required exams Step 2: Crack the respective exam of a college/university in order to secure admission to the course. Step 3: After the entrances are over successfully, the college announces the result and releases a list of shortlisted students Step 4: Shortlisted candidates then need to go through the college wise admission process. Step 5: Seats are finally allotted to the students in the last step of admission. Candidates are then required to deposit the fee for the course and get registered under the respective colleges for that academic session. What are the MSc Microbiology Eligibility Criteria? Following are the MSc Microbiology eligibility criteria to be followed by the candidates: Marksheets of classes X and XII are required with a minimum percentage of 50% or more. A Bachelor’s Degree in Microbiology from a recognized university or an equivalent with a minimum mark of 55% or more. As cracking the entrances are essential for admission, so apply to the entrance exams. Start preparing for the entrance exam as soon as possible so that the maximum syllabus is covered efficiently. Note that the sections of the entrances are usually of bachelors level. Check some of the basic topics for MSc Microbiology entrances below: Bacteria Fungi Viruses Immune System Enzyme Technology DNA Technology Start preparing notes and maintain a separate notebook for all the valuable topics. This will be a great help in revising all the concepts easily before the exam. Solve as many as question papers possible as it is mandatory to understand the exam pattern clearly. MSc in Biochemistry is a 2-year postgraduate program that allows you to understand the chemical processes related to living organisms. This course contains a mixture of biology and chemistry. To pursue this course you need to clear 10+2+3 with a minimum aggregate score of 45-50%. You need to qualify the entrance exams too for securing admissions in this course. There are a number of national and college-level entrance exams for which you can apply to lock seats in this course like Amity JEE, GSAT, Pantnagar University Entrance Examination, BHU-PET, and other exams. See Also: MSc Biochemistry Syllabus There is a pool of colleges and universities offering this course. This course is a research-oriented course that enables you to have hands-on experiments, practical labs, and theoretical thesis. It involves the study of subjects like Immunology, Cell Biology, Bioinformatics, Enzymology, and alike. An average fee charged for this course is up to INR 1 Lakh per annum. The course fee varies from institute to institute depending upon the facilities they offer. After successfully completing this course you can apply for a pool of lucrative job positions like associate engineers, research scientists, professors, research biochemists, regional managers, and other similar positions. MSc Biochemistry full form is a Master of Science degree in Biochemistry subject. It is a 2-year post-graduation course that allows you to get detailed knowledge of subjects related to biochemistry and its related domains like cell biology, immunology, microbiology, bioinformatics and etc. Biochemistry mainly aims to provide an understanding of the structure and functioning of living things. This course deals with genetic engineering, bioinformatics, and molecular biology. This program fosters critical thinking and problem-solving skills to prepare candidates for dynamic environments and challenges. The main focus of this course is to train candidates for the emerging field of biochemistry. Give exposure to practical and theory subjects. Why Study MSc Biochemistry? There are numerous reasons to pursue this course. Few of those reasons are listed below which will definitely convince you to opt for this course: It provides candidates with diverse and dynamic job opportunities. You will be exposed to high paid jobs in both the public and private sectors. More exciting and adventurous opportunities await them in biochemical firms. You can also avail of scholarships through this course. Due to advancements and rapid growth in this sector, MSc Biochemistry graduates are in huge demand. Enhance your communication, technical and problem-solving skills. You will get to learn technical terms related to your jobs and the protocols correlated to the same. You can look out for solutions here by experimenting with things. MSc Biochemistry Admission Process Admissions in MSc Biochemistry can be procured on the basis of both merit and entrance exam. There are a variety of exam scores that colleges accept for offering admissions. Moreover, once the applications are released, you can easily apply for these courses. To apply for this course you need to follow the below-mentioned steps: You need to either visit the admission office or the official website of the college to avail the application form. Then you need to fill the application form by furnishing DOB, contact details, educational qualifications, identity proofs, signatures, and etc. Lastly and finally, you need to make the final application fee payment. If you are applying for the college, that is offering admissions on the basis of entrance exams then you need to apply for those entrance exams too. Also, ensure that you meet the minimum educational eligibility criteria with minimum required marks. MSc Biochemistry Eligibility To secure admission in this course, you need to befit the eligibility criteria for the same. Few of those eligibility qualifications are discussed below, you can check here that whether you are qualified for this course or not: Must have qualified their 10+2 from a recognized board or equivalent. Should have secured a minimum aggregate score of 50% in the BSc degree course or equivalent. You might have to appear and qualify national and state level entrance examinations to secure admissions. Make sure that you score above 45% in these entrance examinations to lock your admission seats in good colleges. Candidates between the age of 17-21 years, can apply for this course. MSc Biochemistry Entrance Exams To acquire admissions in the MSc Biochemistry course you have to appear for National and College-level entrance exams like BHU-PET, GSAT, Amity JEE, AIIMS Biochemistry entrance exams, and other exams. Few of those important entrance exams are discussed below with their important dates and details: Name of the Exams Registration Dates (Tentative) Exam Dates (Tentative) NPAT December 2023 – May 21, 2024 January 2024 – May 2024 CUET February 2024 – April 2024 May 15 - 31, 2024 CUCET November 28, 2023 - May 29, 2024 May 2024 SET January 2024 May 2024 How to Prepare for MSc Biochemistry Entrance Exams? To prepare for these entrance exams you need to do very well. Few of the common preparation steps are discussed below: Prepare a time table to timely finish the syllabus. Refer to the previous year’s question papers and solved mock test papers. Go through the topics of Bachelor’s degree subjects. Mostly, these topics include general science, cell biology, and immunology questions but as per previous year question papers, it also includes questions from metabolism, cancer biology, and bioenergetic related questions. How to get admission in a good MSc Biochemistry college? Keep track of updates and notifications of the colleges you are applying for. Secure good marks and ranks in entrance examinations. Prepare properly for the entrance examinations. MSc Biochemistry Syllabus MSc in Biochemistry is a postgraduate course of 2 years that comprises 4 semesters. The course curriculum comprises subjects related to biotechnology, bioinformatics, immunology, cell biology, and similar. syllabus.text: M.Sc Biochemistry Syllabus M.Sc in Biochemistry course is a 2 year postgraduate program divided into 4 semesters. The syllabus of this program focuses on covering methods to understand the chemical processes related to living organisms. It also deals with the study of chemical procedures in living organisms. Tabulated below is the syllabus of M.Sc Biochemistry explained in detail. Semester I Semester II Cell Biology and Physiology Methods of Molecular Biology Biomolecules and Microbial Biochemistry Bioenergetics and Metabolism I Bioanalytical Techniques Metabolism II Nutritional Biochemistry Immunology Bio Organic Preparations and Analytical Biochemistry Bioanalytical techniques - Microbiology and Immunology Semester III Semester IV Enzymology Neurobiochemistry Plant Biochemistry Outlines of Biotechnology Clinical Biochemistry Enzymology and Enzyme Technology Molecular biology Assignment based Seminar Biochemical Preparations and Clinical Biochemistry Project Work Including Presentation, Comprehensive Viva M.Sc Biochemistry Subjects M.Sc in Biochemistry is a 2 year postgraduate program that includes a mixture of theory and practical subjects along with project work. The syllabus might vary in different colleges but more or less it is the same. How to Become a Biotechnologist How to Become a Biotechnologist MSc Biochemistry First Year Subjects Cell Biology and Physiology: This subject as the name suggests is related to cells and their functionality covering areas such as cell biology, blood, digestive system, respiration, excretory system, endocrine etc. Biomolecules and Microbial Biochemistry: This subject is divided into two sections- one part is Biomolecules which includes carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, enzymes, nucleic acids etc and the other part is microbial Biochemistry which includes morphology, bacterial toxins, viruses etc. Bioanalytical TechniQues. These subjects guide candidates about Spectroscopy, Chromatography, centrifugation, electrophoretic techniques, viscosity, X-ray diffraction, X-ray absorption, NMR etc. Medical Courses Clinical Research Courses MSc Biochemistry Second Year Subjects Methods in Molecular Biology: This subject is one of the core subjects in semester II which is a total of 100 marks. The subjects include the following such as chromatin, Genes, Mutation, Recombinant DNA methods, DNA sequencing etc. Bioenergetics and Metabolism I: The subjects are bioenergetics relating to free energy and understanding the relation between equilibrium constant and free energy change. This subject is divided into various aspects such as Bioenergetics, Coenzymes and cofactors, intermediary metabolism, carbohydrates, amino acids etc. Immunology: This subject is also one of the main core subjects in the program. The subjects provide knowledge relating to the immune system such as cells involved in immune responses, the nature of antigens and antibodies, immune effector mechanisms, measurement of antigen-antibody interactions etc. Bioinformatics Courses Biomedical Engineering Courses MSc Biochemistry Third Year Subjects Enzymology: This subject includes kinetics of enzyme action, use of initial velocity, reversible and irreversible inhibition, mechanism of Enzyme action, acid-base catalysis, covalent catalysis, alcohol dehydrogenase, aldolase, enzyme regulation, product inhibition etc. Plant Biochemistry: Plant Biochemistry is a subject as the name suggest is related to plants and it includes Electron transport system in plants, nitrate assimilation, Photosynthesis, toxins of plant origin, stress metabolism in plants, etc. Clinical Biochemistry: This subject is related to bodily disorders and various type of diseases such as disorders of carbohydrate metabolism, disorders of lipids, inborn errors of Metabolism, digestive diseases, disorders of liver and kidney, electrolytes and acid-base, diagnostic enzymes etc. Medical Microbiology Courses Medical Biotechnology Courses MSc Biochemistry Fourth Semester Subjects Neurobiochemistry: This subject is related to neurobiochemistry which has different dimensions to it and it includes Muscle Biochemistry, neuron morphology, neurophysiology, neurological disorders etc. Outlines of Biotechnology: This subject is one of the elective subjects that the candidates can choose. The geographers are taught both the physical properties of the earth’s surface and the human societies spread across it. The course helps to develop skills in geographic information science, cartography, remote sensing, fluvial geomorphology, and world language. They bring together the physical dimensions of the world with the human side of things and thus help to minimize the negative human impact on the environment. Geographers are required to help find solutions to some of the biggest issues in the world, such as climate change, urban over-development, natural disasters, etc. With the development of human society, global issues are increasing and thus the employment opportunities are also growing exponentially. syllabus.text: MSc Psychology Syllabus Semester I Semester II Cognitive Psychology I Theory Cognitive Psychology-II Theory Statistics in Behavioural Sciences Theory Experimental Designs Theory Research Methods in Psychology Theory Psychometrics Theory Neuro Psychology I Theory Neuro Psychology I Theory Optional: Group (A) – Psychopathology Group (B) – Guidance and Counselling Psychology Group (C) – Principles of Organizational Behaviour Optional: Group (A) – Psycho diagnostics and Assessment Group (B) – Special Areas of Counselling Group (C) – Organizational Dynamics Practical Practical Seminar Seminar Semester III Semester IV Psychology of Social Behaviour Theory Dynamics and Interpersonal Behaviour Theory Applications of Psychology I Theory Applications of Psychology-II Theory Personality Theory Self and Positive Psychology Systems and Skills Intervention in Psychology I Theory Systems and Skills Intervention in Psychology – II Theory Optional: Group (A) – Perspectives in Mental Health Group (B) – Therapeutics in Counselling Group (C) - Engineering Psychology Optional: Group (A) – Psychological Treatment of Mental Disorders Group (B) – Assessment in Guidance and Counselling Group (C) – Issues in Industrial Psychology Synopsis Research Project/Dissertation MSc Psychology Subjects MSc Psychology subjects are divided into 4 semesters. The important subjects of each year are mentioned below: MSc Psychology First Year Subjects Cognitive Psychology I Theory: Cognitive psychology focuses on the science of how people think. M.Sc. in Forensic Sciences is a 2-year full-time post-graduate course that is divided into 4 semesters. Forensics is a method used to determine what happened before, during, and after a crime. Students can choose to focus on one area of forensics, such as Biology or Cyber Security, relevant to the sort of criminal activity to detect. The course may also involve an advanced study of Psychology for understanding a criminal’s mind. The course prepares students to detect dicey situations where a crime may occur, such as cyber security, towards preventing digital attacks before they can happen. Even handwriting analysis can be used in marital counseling and to help someone choose a career path. See Also: Forensic Science Courses There are multiple universities and colleges offering Forensic Science degrees. The course prepares candidates for professional roles in Forensic Science, such as police or forensic practice, the criminal or civil justice system or research. They can develop command, control, and management skills that will enable them to present expert evidential incident reports to the court of law. Certificate Courses in Forensic Science Forensic Pathology The average annual course fee in India ranges between INR 20,000 and 2 lacs, depending upon the institute offering the course. Information and details about the MSc Geology course are as follows. This course describes ‘Geology’ and identifies some of its main principles and identifies the main branches of geology. In this course, students will get to study Earth Sciences concerned with the solid earth, the rocks of which it is composed, and the process by which they change over time. The MSc Geology program also includes the study of the solid features of any terrestrial planet or natural satellite such as Mars or the Moon. A course in Geology is concerned with the understanding and learning of how the entire system of Earth does its work. It includes the landforms, various processes, constituents and history. MSc Geology course encompasses the study of various layers of the earth from prehistoric times to the contemporary time, it also assesses the evolution throughout the years. It provides students with a detailed insight into the diverse processes of the atmosphere and the evolution of life. Why Study MSc Geology? There are so many reasons why an individual should pursue an MSc Geology course. Students can pursue this course because of the following benefits of the course: This course prepares students for other careers in business, law, education and others. A course in Geology gives you a good insight and appreciation of natural forces and everything that we see around us, plus a realistic grasp of time (i.e. geological time) as applied to everything else in Science. Some of the common job profiles for the MSc Geology postgraduates are Project Assistant, Geologist, Geological Technologists, Assistant Geologist, Geo-Scientist, Assistant Chemist, Hydro Geologist, ONGC Chair Professor etc. The students also have the opportunity to carry out research works in their field. There are a lot of research labs in India that appoints MSc Geology students for carrying out their research. The MSc Geology salary package ranges between INR 2,00,000 and 13,00,000 annually. The salary largely depends on the job profile for which they have been appointed. What is the MSc Geology Admission Process? Some of the major all India entrance exams conducted for this purpose are BHU PET, IIT JAM, DUET etc. Some colleges also offer admission on merit basis. Submit documents: Scan and upload all required documents like mark sheets. Documents need to be uploaded in a specific format only, as specified by the institute’s application portal. Application fee: A minimal application fee is to be paid online during the submission of the application form. Payment can be done by all online payment modes. Download admit card: Admit cards are released once all applicants are judged for eligibility. The admit card must be downloaded and printed out to be used on the day of the examination. Examination: Prepare for the exam as per the syllabus and past papers. Appear for the examination on the date announced. Results: Based on candidates performance in the entrance exam, results will be announced. What is the MSc Geology Eligibility Criteria? MSc Electronics has immense placement opportunities both national and foreign based. The foreign based opportunities are not only for employment but also for higher studies are extremely appreciable. Pay the required fees and confirm the submission of the application form. If the college or university chooses to intake students on merit basis, with the aggregate marks secured in the undergraduate program, mail or message will be sent to the contact number mentioned in the application form and you will be called for counselling and can pay the fees and get an admission in the college. An admit card is a mandatory document to be carried to the exam hall. The students can prepare for the exam and appear for the same. The results will be published in the official website on the mentioned date by the college. One can check the results and take counselling and pay the required fees, submit the required documents and get an admission in the college or university. Why Study MSc Home Science? MSc Home Science has multiple benefits, some of which are listed below. Moreover, it deals with planning and Management of the production activities taking food safety and quality of the product into account. To be eligible to apply for this program, candidates should hold a Bachelor’s degree in relevant discipline from a recognized university with an aggregate of at least 50% marks. Admissions will be based on the candidate’s performance in the entrance exam. However, some institutes/ universities also offer admission based on merit i,e the marks scored by the candidate in Bachelor’s degree examination. The average tuition fee charged in India for MSc Food Technology course ranges between INR 5,000 and INR 2,00,000 for a period of two years, depending on the university/ college offering the course. Food Technology is the branch of Food Science that involves the processing, preservation, preparation, selection. On completion of this course, candidates can easily get a job as etc.a dietician, food technologist, production manager, food packaging manager, etc. with an average initial salary package ranging between INR 25,000 and INR 75,000 per month. MSc Food Technology is a 2-year postgraduate program that deals with the technologies to produce, preserve, process, package, and distribute the food. It includes the study of processes and techniques involved from collecting the raw material to reaching the final product to the consumer. The aim of the course is to reduce the amount of food waste that has been seen in every step of food processing and distribution. The course also focuses on producing a high-quality product, maintaining the nutrition value of the food, increasing the shelf life of the product, and availability of the seasonal fruits and vegetables throughout the year. The course imparts knowledge and skills to deal with the technicalities and diverse issues with the food processing technologies. The program covers subjects like Food Microbiology, Packaging Technology, Dairy Technology, Food Chemistry, Physical, Microbiological & Chemical structure of food, Designing and production of foods with its health benefits, Food Chemistry, Food Processing, Surface and Colloidal Chemistry, Microbiology, Nutrition and Analysis of Food. The graduates can get jobs in various organizations such as the Food Corporation of India, Modern Food Corporation, North-Eastern Agricultural Marketing Corporation. They can also get an opportunity to become Research Scientists and pursue advanced research in the relative field. This course also provides skills to the students to work as a Food Technologist in popular food processing firms which in turn helps them to grow as a technical professional. Why study MSc Food Technology? There are many benefits to pursuing MSc Food Technology degree program. Some of them are: Food industries have been introducing a lot of new technologies and tools to produce products according to the changing lifestyle of the people. With the advancement in the industries, the requirement of skilled professionals is quite high. Food is a basic requirement and thus food industries are one of the rising industries in every country. So the MSc Food Tech graduates can get numerous entry-level jobs in Marketing or Quality Assurance Companies, Production Management Firms, Logistics Department, Research and Development Centers, Hotels and Restaurants, Colleges and Universities, etc. There is also a great opportunity to learn and grow both on professional and personal terms in this sector. The average salary that one can expect as a fresher in this sector is around INR 7,00,000. Students can also pursue jobs as a Dietician, Food Technologist, etc. in various govt. or private organizations. Those who wish to pursue higher studies in the field of Food Technology can also pursue a Ph.D. in this field and can easily get a higher position in the public and private sector. Based on the marks obtained in the Bachelor’s degree examination and personal interview, candidates will be shortlisted for further admission rounds. Candidates should have BSc Food Technology/ B.Sc Food Science and Technology/ BSc in Dairy Technology/ B.Tech Food Technology or any equivalent field like Life science, Biotechnology, Microbiology, Chemistry, Biology, Home Science, etc. They should have scored at least 50% aggregate marks in their bachelor’s degree. They are actually trying to ensure that the proper nutrition is delivered to the patients with kidney diseases, diabetes, heart diseases, obesity and more. They work for any health organizations, hospitals, clinics to offer proper nutritional counselling to the patients by improving their diet chart.

Study of insects, both in the natural habitat and under controlled situations in the lab is the work of an entomologist. They observe life stages and migration patterns, and also check out the movement and habits of insects within the urban environment, including businesses and households. Information that they discover is shared with health professionals in an attempt to extend public safety and reduce the incidence of direct and indirect harm to the human population.

Forensic Entomologists make an accurate estimation for how long a person has been dead because different types of insects are attracted to different stages of decomposition. Life stages of eggs and young insects can also expel out important clues. They must take certain environmental factors under consideration when examining bodies, season, ambient temperature, time of day, and also the surroundings of the body. These factors affect a body's rate of decomposition, and bug growth.

MSc Applied Mathematics is a course of advanced studies in the stream of mathematics. It includes studying deeply the main areas of mathematical techniques, their analysis and implementation as well as derivation of values to determine various equations. This course is divided in two parts: numerical analysis and industrial modeling techniques. Former one (numeric analysis) is a course that determines the various algorithms of various problems of mathematics, this part of the subject helps a student in applying these algorithms into the recent industries for their better computation and helping them grow in their course. The latter or industrial modeling techniques focus mainly on the industrial plane as it teaches students how to apply their knowledge in bettering the industrial output by applying mathematics and statistics to draw conclusions. This stream is gaining more pace and is widely known which in turn is getting more and more people joining in to gain more experience and expertise in this work line. This program essentially prepares a student to design, develop, and understand various mathematics equations and algorithms for their application in the physical world. How these equations through their sophisticated approach can better existing industries and resources. Why Study MSc Applied Mathematics? As each day passes by, the world is witnessing a sharp revolution in its economic and scientific policies, with increase in demands of all sorts; the need to revolutionize new industries and better the existing ones has become important. Therefore to embrace globalization and constant changes that occur in the industrial world. Knowledge of Applied Mathematics is required to study these problems in a scientific manner. Applied mathematics is a course specially designed to apply the universal laws of mathematics in the conventional world to derive a conclusion and to avert any crisis. Applied mathematics studies mathematical techniques and analysis, and its main focus is to apply that theoretical and numerical knowledge into the world and its issues. To tackle them with the help of science and better our resources for the long run MSc in Applied Mathematics is a holistic course that imparts knowledge firstly by making students understand the process of a numerical and their abilities and secondly how these mathematical techniques can be applied in the practical world to seek reformation and revival of new and existing industries. This particular course due to its extensive and in-depth curriculum is applicable in all industrial areas. Graduates of this degree can get hired to design and apply their mathematical know how into current industrial scenario for its betterment Sectors that are related to engineering and manufacturing are always in need of personnel that are keen and help in designing various theories in applications of their machinery work. Hence Applied Mathematics graduates can also get hired by such employers Candidates who are interested in working in banking sectors and National treasuries of India can also venture into such professions with ease and provide their insight on matters related to such organizations Post-graduation degree holders can also work as teachers and assistants in various colleges and institutions and earn handsome money and packages Candidates interested in working as CA and CS in accounting firms are also welcome as they have regular need for professionals with a good mathematical background to handle matters of financial fervor. This degree is also beneficial on a personal level, candidates can get an analytical bent of mind with their logical and statistical strength on point. Applied mathematics is universally accepted and offers appealing job opportunities internationally as well. What is the MSc Applied Mathematics Admission Process? The admission in this course is done through entrance exams. Candidates are required to have a graduate degree with mathematics as a major which is asked by several colleges in order to get admission in their master’s program. Industrial Chemistry is a futuristic approach to development of goods and products as many high-end industries rely heavily on chemical processes to produce various outputs such as perfumes, medicines, petrochemical and agricultural goods to contribute alternatives to such organizations and provide stability and assistance in their growth and expansion. Industrial Chemistry aspirants may seek employment opportunities with such organizations as research associates and taxonomist as well as scientists and pharmacists and gain recognition for their work in transitioning and transformations of various chemicals into finished products such as medicines, agricultural fertilizers and pesticides as well as perfumes and petrochemicals products to ensure usage of chemically induced products which are sustainable and provide better outcomes. Industrial Chemistry aspirants have many options in regards to their employment areas; candidates can actively work with educational institutions and organizations as research associates and contribute their work in discovering interactive tendencies of various chemicals to procure suitable results as well as preparation of reports to discover hazardous elements. Candidates can also work in leading perfume industries as experts in preparation of incense and aromatic scents for sale, as well as contribute insights as pharmacist and chemist into building chemical composition essential for medicine making and testing compatibility of various chemicals with one another to create harmonious and nonhazardous products. Students are directly exposed to various modern aspects of ongoing global activities from the beginning. This course is a combination of biology at the microorganism level as well as at the level of human beings. Students are required to study organisms and microorganisms at the molecular and physiological levels. This course has a particular area of concentration in which the course offering will focus on the specific topic and which will result in the students having an in-depth and comprehensive knowledge base. This includes instruction on the classification and composition of non-carbon molecules, including their structure and bonding properties, conductivity and reactivity, scientific techniques such as spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and photoelectron analysis. The course also deals with the study of particular compounds such as transition metals and inorganic and organic molecular compounds. MSc Inorganic Chemistry is structured and designed in a manner so as to develop academic base through semester-wise theoretical examination while developing the practical skills through lab modules, experiments, and research. MSc Inorganic Chemistry has applications throughout every field of the chemical industry that include catalysis, materials science, pigments, surfactants, coatings, medicine, gasoline and agriculture throughout every field of the chemical industry. Candidates also hold the opportunity to explore the industrial, pharmaceutical, technological and commercial fields of chemistry as the course basically concentrates on the uses of chemistry in modern society. M.Sc. genetics is a specialized postgraduate course for students who are seeking to get a postgraduate degree in genetics. Masters in genetics is about studies on living organisms down to their genetic level. Students get to study about the various techniques, procedures that are involved in performing a genetic level experiment or to study the genomic makeup of a particular organism. The curriculum is made in such a way so that the students get to study all the latest techniques and procedures that are to be carried out in a high profile laboratory in order to perform any experiment. DNA isolation, DNA fingerprinting, DNA sequencing, details about genomic marker studies, etc. are some of the important technical knowledge that is incorporated in the course. See Also: MSc Genetics Colleges in India The average fee charged by colleges who offer these M.Sc. genetics ranges from INR 5000 to 2 Lacs per annum. It can vary depending upon the college the student has chosen. The fees vary from private to government colleges. Those who don’t want to pursue any higher degree can apply for various public and private sector jobs. Job roles such as Professor, research scientists, Senior Scientific Officer – Molecular Genetics, Technical Assistant - Molecular Genetics, Associate Professor - Medical Genetics, National Sales Manager – Genetics, Sales & Marketing Executive, Principal Plant Breeder – Cotton, Partner Account Manager are some of the common career options. The average salary that one can expect after completing M.Sc. genetics ranges from INR 2 lacs to 8 lacs per annum depending on the job roles. For students who choose to pursue the course from distance, the duration may depend on the college. Students who have successfully completed their undergraduate degree in microbiology, biotechnology, genetics, or any other life science subject from a recognized board of education are eligible for the postgraduate course of M.Sc. genetics. Most of the universities take admissions based on cut-offs, but some might ask for entrance exams. Why Study MSc Genetics? There are many benefits of pursuing an MSc in genetics. Some of them are: Students will gain an in-depth knowledge of the genetic level work that is going on in the world and learn those techniques so that they can implement them in their own research. With the rise of more and more diseases, studying at the genetic level and finding a cure for that is also becoming important, hence this is quite a flourishing field. Placement is not like all other courses where companies come and recruit. Step 4 – The shortlisted students from the interview round will get admission. Geophysics is a stream that is a combination of two important core subjects i.e. Physics and Geography. The two subjects and their integrated learning is known as Geophysics which has become an important subject to learn the basics of Earth Science and to procure more information on earth's natural surface. This degree imparts knowledge on earth's natural surface and resources through the study of quantitative physical methods that are making extensive use of Physics in studying various natural phenomena such as seismic activity, electromagnetic waves, and radioactivity. The earth's crust and core are subjected to numerous changes that are responsible for many natural activities that still need to be investigated thoroughly, therefore Geophysics is the field that offers answers to such questions and conducts active research and analysis on these important activities. The stream also provides information on the structural alignment and composition of the earth by exploring the earth's surface and investigating how the earth was formed and the functional forces behind this formation. The stream also applies the concepts of Physics to understand the geological point of view of earth's formation and to derive answers for the same. Such crucial knowledge of earth can further lead us to find how important minerals, oil, and stones are formulated to ensure the protection of naturally occurring resources. Candidates can also become exploration advisors in geological organizations and can assist the main advisor in the preparation of reports and information on different aspects of the earth's formation. Candidates can also pursue a research career and can carry out their independent ventures or research proposals and can also get paid. The candidates can also visit the important geological places for data analysis and specimen collection. Candidates are always welcome to pursue a career as a teacher or a professor in a College or a University and also conduct research and publish it in journals for a successful career in teaching. Candidates can also seek employment as Scientists in Agricultural Laboratories and Institutions to study soil formation and fertility of the earth's surface. MSc Toxicology is a field which deals with the study of toxins and other harmful chemical substances which have an adverse effect on human and other living organisms. Students will learn about the relationship between doses and their effect on the exposed organisms It is a subfield of bioscience. MSc Toxicology involves observing and reporting symptoms, mechanisms, detection, and treatments of toxic substances, in particular relation to the poisoning in humans. It includes environmental agents and chemical compounds found in nature, as well as pharmaceutical compounds that are synthesized for medical use by humans The course was developed in such a way that after completion of the degree students have the knowledge about the toxins, their mode of action, detection, and treatment. The students seeking admission to MSc Toxicology can choose various specialization subjects also like forensic toxicology, medical toxicology, occupational toxicology, aquatic toxicology, environmental toxicology, etc. Students choosing this subject should have good analytical and logical thinking skills. Good hand-eye coordination is also very important during the analysis of toxins. After completion of this degree students can opt for higher studies by choosing Ph.D they can work in research laboratories, hospitals, government organizations. After successful registration candidates have to fill the online application form with all the relevant required details (personal details, academic details). After filling up the details upload the required photo and signature in the portal. Click on “next” and proceed further. Pay the required registration fees and click on “submit” for the final submission of the registration form. Print out the fees receipt and application form for future reference. MSc Dietetics: What is it About? MSc Dietetics is quite popular nowadays and can be described in the following points:- MSc in Dietetics is a scientific study of food and body with the aim of inculcating the knowledge about various nutrients, their effect on the body, amount required or types of problems associated with excess or lack of any particular nutritional component in the body. It helps to prepare a proper diet chart as per the need and requirement of a body to maintain a healthy lifestyle and curb diseases. The course covers all the aspects of interactions and living body mechanism with ingestion of any consumable or lack of nutrition in the body. The curriculum is designed in a way to inculcate the mechanical, biochemical, physical, and bioelectrical aspects of the food on the body. Students can go for higher studies to pursue PhD Dietetics or MPhil Dietetics. Why Study MSc Dietetics? MSc Dietetics offers various perks for the students including a good package, interesting job profile, etc. Below are some points which make MSc Dietetics worth choosing:- MSc in Dietetics course is popular worldwide with many job opportunities. Students after completing this course work on providing proper dietary plans to people teaching the healthy eating importance. The extensive knowledge of this course can help people to teach the world the importance of healthy eating and nutrition for the body developing some diet charts properly as per their needs. This course opens up doors to work for some interesting job roles like Clinical Dietician, Consultant Dietician, Nutrition Product Manager and more. MSc dietetics also enables a candidate to employ as a self-practitioner or join any private or government hospital as a consultant with high salary packages. MSc Audio Speech Therapy in India is a full time 2 years long masters program inclusive of 4 semesters which are scheduled for 6 months each. As middlemen, Export Managers plan and coordinate the international shipment of goods. They negotiate with a variety of people, such as shippers, agents and vendors, and are expected to have excellent customer service skills in dealing with customers. They may also have to ensure that shipments are in compliance with the laws and regulations governing the export industry.

Relationship Managers are responsible for identifying the key staff in client companies to cultivate profitable relationships. They ensure that customer complaints are resolved quickly and effectively. Also, they forward upselling and cross-selling opportunities to the sales teams. They also promote high-quality sales, supply and customer service processes, and work to retain customers and renew contracts. They approach potential customers to establish beneficial trade relationships, and conduct business reviews to ensure that clients are satisfied with their products and services. Also, they update the CRM and ensure that Account Managers are aware of significant client-related changes.

Since a key component of this job is strategic planning, a Business Development Manager must have a thorough knowledge of the company's competitors and the marketplace. They work closely with the sales and marketing departments to identify potential new clients, craft proposals, and review contracts.

Foreign Trade Analysts are responsible for international business analysis, and overseeing the transfer of products and services between countries all across the globe. Foreign Trade Analysts track the exchange of goods and services between nations in an increasingly interconnected world. They work in both private and public sectors because various companies and government entities have an interest in understanding international markets.

Foreign Trade and Purchasing Specialists are responsible for coordinating credit and financial activities and obtaining payments for import/export operations. They act as advisors on matters of tariffs, markets, and federal and foreign regulations. Also, they ensure that all filings, documents, and regulatory reporting are completed accurately, in a timely manner, and according to trade laws. They maintain information of international events and changes to laws and requirements that may impact operations. Additionally, they negotiate letters of credit or handle issues with international banks.

Supply Chain Managers select transportation routes to maximize economy by combining shipments or consolidating warehousing and distribution. They develop material costs forecasts or standard cost lists. Also, they assess appropriate material handling equipment needs and staffing levels to load, unload, move, or store materials.

Market Research Executives help identify what people do, think, buy or believe and why. Market Research Executives are responsible for consulting clients about project requirements and objectives, designing research methods such as interviews and questionnaires. They carry out qualitative or quantitative research, approve timescales and budgets, supervise staff, monitor work progress. They also write reports, including client recommendations, and analyse, translate, and present results. They also advise clients on how they can best make use of such results.

Developmental Studies is a 2- year full- time course divided into 4 semesters, with each semester lasting a period of 6 months. A developmental study is a university program classified under the discipline of Social Sciences. For most universities, the program also encompasses units that cover International Relations. The course curriculum focuses on three key areas affecting mankind, namely social, economic and political sectors. Different development policies that have had impacts on and helped shape the community, both locally and internationally, often form the point of scrutiny for the students enrolled in this program. The course aims to enable students to develop a critical awareness of the society. Students who graduate with this degree find professional careers in academic institutions pursuing inter disciplinary research and teaching the specialization of Development Studies in civil and allied administrative services.
